A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework and TextHalu-Bench contribution. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, hallucination-attention correlations, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative model outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds generalization results and quantitative localization and attention-variation analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same Glimpse/Refocus procedure, grounded-layer selection, three correction strategies, and default weighted fusion. Revised hallucination-scoring prose clarifies probability extraction without establishing a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix E, Table 5 adds evaluated coverage on MME-P, MME-VideoOCR, and A-OKVQA, extending the evidence to broader perception, video-text understanding, and knowledge-dependent question answering. Existing scene-text and generalization benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The existing LMM, adversarial-training, CoT, and external-text-detector comparisons are retained. The new localization experiment in Appendix F, Table 9 explicitly compares a final-layer top-k attention baseline and a Glimpse-only variant against the complete ZoomText procedure, adding a limited diagnostic comparison.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an IoU evaluation using 100 manually annotated samples from TextHalu-Bench, TextVQA, and ST-VQA, plus foreground/background attention-CV measurements. Section 4 also changes the reported benchmark size from 1,730 to 1,740 without explaining the difference or establishing that existing evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix F analyses directly test two central ZoomText premises: progressive improvement in spatial localization and greater cross-layer attention variation for foreground than background tokens. These add mechanistic evidence beyond the retained downstream-performance ablations. The qualitative comparison also replaces some v1 examples with new cases in Figure 6.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars; v2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars. The new attention-CV analysis measures variation across layers, not uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets while retaining the main table's reported scores. New Table 5 baseline/method values are 1567.7/1572.2 on MME-P, 59.2/60.8 on MME-VideoOCR, and 85.2/85.6 on A-OKVQA. Table 9 adds localization and attention-variation findings, including Qwen2.5-VL IoU scores of 46.1, 48.9, and 52.7 across successive variants. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and the underlying mathematical formulation remain unchanged, with no added theorem, proof, or derivation. New Equation 7 states the standard coefficient-of-variation formula for an empirical diagnostic rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about semantic hallucination, attention grounding, the training-free ZoomText/GLC framework, and TextHalu-Bench. Added experiments support these existing contributions; the benchmark-count revision does not redefine their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds an interpretation connecting foreground/background CV differences to identifying stable attention 'sink tokens' and supporting Refocus. It also interprets localization gains as evidence for the two-stage grounding strategy. Existing limitations concerning computational overhead and dependence on the base model's OCR ability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 clarifies extracting candidate-token probabilities from the next-token distribution. Appendix F documents quadrilateral annotations, localization variants, and token grouping for the new diagnostics. The checklist adds a code/data release-upon-acceptance statement, while the project link, main hyperparameters, hardware descriptions, and existing baseline implementation details remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds six cited works: VidText, EarthMind, VideoEspresso, MME, MME-VideoOCR, and A-OKVQA. These modestly expand contextual coverage and document added benchmarks; the positioning relative to OCR methods and hallucination mitigation remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory edits, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments and the NeurIPS checklist, and introduces a main-text Visualization section in place of Appendix G. Most scientific prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 5, adds the two-part Table 9 and benchmark-example Figure 7, and moves a revised qualitative panel into main-text Figure 6. That panel retains two of v1 Figure 8's cases, omits four, and adds two. Existing methodological figures and quantitative plots largely retain their displays, with local resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: The new localization and attention-variation analyses provide direct support for previously motivated ZoomText assumptions, while Table 5 broadens generalization evidence. These strengthen the paper without changing its central method or headline results. The unexplained benchmark-size revision and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit the gains; the overall improvement is useful but bounded.
